subproblem.title: Borel majorant of the slice covering sums of one cover (Eilenberg intervals)
subproblem.statement: Let X be an extended metric space, m ∈ ℕ, f : X → ℝ, L ∈ [0, ∞) and A ⊆ X such that f is L-Lipschitz on A (edist(f x, f y) ≤ L·edist(x, y) for x, y ∈ A), and let S_i ⊆ A (i ∈ ℕ). Then there is a Borel function ψ : ℝ → [0, ∞] such that Σ_i ⨆_{S_i ∩ (A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≠ ∅} (ediam(S_i ∩ (A ∩ f⁻¹{t})))^m ≤ ψ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ, and ∫_ℝ ψ dλ¹ ≤ 2L·Σ_i ⨆_{S_i ≠ ∅} (ediam S_i)^{m+1}. The exponents are the real casts of the natural numbers m and m + 1, ediam is the extended diameter, and λ¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [EMetricSpace X] (m : ℕ) (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (A : Set X) (S : ℕ → Set X), LipschitzOnWith L f A → (∀ i, S i ⊆ A) → ∃ ψ : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable ψ ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (S i ∩ (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})).Nonempty), ediam (S i ∩ (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})) ^ (m : ℝ) ≤ ψ t) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ψ t ≤ 2 * (L : ℝ≥0∞) * ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (S i).Nonempty), ediam (S i) ^ ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. X is an extended metric space; no measurable structure on X is used. ediam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter `Metric.ediam S` (written `ediam` under `open Metric`); ediam ∅ = 0. Arithmetic is in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0; x^a for x ∈ [0, ∞] and real a is `ENNReal.rpow`. For S ⊆ X and a real exponent a put w_a(S) := ⨆_{S ≠ ∅} (ediam S)^a, the supremum over the proposition S ≠ ∅, so w_a(S) = (ediam S)^a if S ≠ ∅ and w_a(∅) = 0 (in particular w_0(∅) = 0 although (ediam ∅)^0 = 1). For f : X → ℝ, edist on ℝ is edist(a, b) = |a − b| (as an element of [0, ∞]); `LipschitzOnWith L f A` means edist(f x, f y) ≤ L·edist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ A (unfolding the definition, `hf hx hy` gives this inequality). closedEBall(a, ρ) := {s ∈ ℝ : edist(s, a) ≤ ρ} for a ∈ ℝ and ρ ∈ [0, ∞] (`Metric.closedEBall`). λ¹ = volume on ℝ. The exponents m and m+1 are the real casts of natural numbers.

1. (Intervals.) Work classically. For each i with S_i ≠ ∅ choose x_i ∈ S_i (e.g. the chosen element of the nonempty set) and put I_i := closedEBall(f(x_i), L·ediam S_i); if S_i = ∅ put I_i := ∅. Each I_i is closed (`Metric.isClosed_closedEBall`), hence Borel. By `Real.volume_closedEBall`, λ¹(closedEBall(a, ρ)) = 2ρ for every a ∈ ℝ and every ρ ∈ [0, ∞] (including ρ = ∞ and ρ = 0). Hence λ¹(I_i) = 2·(L·ediam S_i) if S_i ≠ ∅, and λ¹(I_i) = λ¹(∅) = 0 if S_i = ∅.

2. (The function.) Put c_i := w_m(S_i) = ⨆_{S_i ≠ ∅} (ediam S_i)^m and ψ(s) := Σ_{i ∈ ℕ} 1_{I_i}(s)·c_i, i.e. ψ = Σ_i (indicator of I_i with constant value c_i). Each summand is the indicator of a Borel set with a constant value, hence measurable (`measurable_const.indicator`); a countable sum of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions is measurable (`Measurable.ennreal_tsum`, or its replacement `Measurable.tsum`). So ψ is Borel.

3. (Pointwise bound.) Fix t ∈ ℝ, write B := A ∩ f⁻¹{t}, and fix i. We show w_m(S_i ∩ B) ≤ 1_{I_i}(t)·c_i. If S_i ∩ B = ∅, the left side is 0. Otherwise choose y ∈ S_i ∩ B, so y ∈ S_i, y ∈ A and f(y) = t. Then S_i ≠ ∅, so x_i ∈ S_i ⊆ A is defined, and by the Lipschitz condition on A and the definition of the diameter,
 edist(t, f(x_i)) = edist(f(y), f(x_i)) ≤ L·edist(y, x_i) ≤ L·ediam S_i
 (`Metric.edist_le_ediam_of_mem`, and monotonicity of multiplication by L, `mul_le_mul_right` in the pinned Mathlib naming). So t ∈ I_i and 1_{I_i}(t)·c_i = c_i = (ediam S_i)^m. Since S_i ∩ B ⊆ S_i, ediam(S_i ∩ B) ≤ ediam S_i (`Metric.ediam_mono`), and x ↦ x^m is monotone on [0, ∞] because m ≥ 0 (`ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow` with `Nat.cast_nonneg`), so w_m(S_i ∩ B) = (ediam(S_i ∩ B))^m ≤ (ediam S_i)^m. Summing over i (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`) gives Σ_i w_m(S_i ∩ (A ∩ f⁻¹{t})) ≤ ψ(t).

4. (Integral.) By monotone convergence for series (`lintegral_tsum`; each summand is measurable, hence a.e.-measurable) and `lintegral_indicator_const`, ∫ ψ dλ¹ = Σ_i c_i·λ¹(I_i). Fix i. If S_i = ∅, the i-th term is c_i·0 = 0 ≤ 2L·w_{m+1}(S_i). If S_i ≠ ∅, put D := ediam S_i ∈ [0, ∞]; then c_i = D^m and by step 1 the i-th term is D^m·(2·(L·D)) = 2L·(D^m·D) = 2L·D^{m+1} = 2L·w_{m+1}(S_i). Here real powers with natural-number exponents agree with monoid powers (`ENNReal.rpow_natCast`: x^((n : ℕ) : ℝ) = x^n), and D^m·D = D^{m+1} (`pow_succ`) holds for every D ∈ [0, ∞], including D = 0 and D = ∞; the rest is commutative-semiring rearrangement in [0, ∞]. Summing (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`) and pulling out the constant (`ENNReal.tsum_mul_left`): ∫ ψ dλ¹ ≤ Σ_i 2L·w_{m+1}(S_i) = 2L·Σ_i ⨆_{S_i ≠ ∅} (ediam S_i)^{m+1}. ∎

Remarks. L = 0 is allowed (then I_i = closedEBall(f(x_i), 0) = {f(x_i)} has measure 0 and both bounds still hold); ediam S_i = ∞ is allowed (λ¹(I_i) = 2·(L·∞) is ∞ if L > 0 and 0 if L = 0, matching `Real.volume_closedEBall`). Only the inclusions S_i ⊆ A (to apply the Lipschitz bound at x_i) and m ≥ 0 are used; no measurability of A, f or S_i is needed.
proof_key_steps: For nonempty S_i pick x_i ∈ S_i and let I_i := closedEBall(f(x_i), L·ediam S_i) (I_i := ∅ otherwise); λ¹(I_i) = 2·L·ediam S_i by Real.volume_closedEBall.
ψ := Σ_i 1_{I_i}·⨆_{S_i≠∅}(ediam S_i)^m is Borel (indicators of closed sets, countable sum).
If S_i ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∋ y then t = f(y) ∈ I_i by the Lipschitz bound, and (ediam(S_i ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹{t}))^m ≤ (ediam S_i)^m; sum termwise.
lintegral_tsum + lintegral_indicator_const: ∫ψ = Σ_i c_i λ¹(I_i) = Σ_i 2L·w_{m+1}(S_i) (rpow_natCast, pow_succ).

audit.reason: The type matches the prose and requires neither coverage of A nor measurability on X. The chosen closed extended balls contain each image by the Lipschitz hypothesis. Their indicators give the pointwise covering bound and a Borel sum. The integral calculation uses the verified extended-ball volume formula and natural-power identity, remaining valid for m = 0, L = 0, empty pieces and infinite diameters. The proof is complete and independent of other children.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure is at most the liminf of covering sums with empty pieces discarded
subproblem.statement: Let X be an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra, let d ∈ ℝ, let s ⊆ X be arbitrary, let r : ℕ → [0, ∞] with r_k → 0, and let T_{k,i} ⊆ X (k, i ∈ ℕ) satisfy ediam T_{k,i} ≤ r_k for all k, i and s ⊆ ⋃_i T_{k,i} for every k. Then μH[d](s) ≤ liminf_{k→∞} Σ_i ⨆_{T_{k,i} ≠ ∅} (ediam T_{k,i})^d, where μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure (outer measure on arbitrary sets) and the supremum over the proposition T_{k,i} ≠ ∅ makes empty pieces contribute 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) (r : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞) (T : ℕ → ℕ → Set X), Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ k i, ediam (T k i) ≤ r k) → (∀ k, s ⊆ ⋃ i, T k i) → (μH[d] : Measure X) s ≤ liminf (fun k => ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (T k i).Nonempty), ediam (T k i) ^ d) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. X is an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra. ediam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter `Metric.ediam S` (written `ediam` under `open Metric`); ediam ∅ = 0. μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) sets. Arithmetic is in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0; x^a for x ∈ [0, ∞] and real a is `ENNReal.rpow`. For S ⊆ X and a real exponent a put w_a(S) := ⨆_{S ≠ ∅} (ediam S)^a, the supremum over the proposition S ≠ ∅, so w_a(S) = (ediam S)^a if S ≠ ∅ and w_a(∅) = 0 (in particular w_0(∅) = 0 although (ediam ∅)^0 = 1).

1. (Discard empty pieces.) For k ∈ ℕ let J_k := {i ∈ ℕ : T_{k,i} ≠ ∅}, regarded as the subtype {i : ℕ // (T k i).Nonempty}; it is countable (a subtype of ℕ), so `Countable (J_k)` holds for every k. Consider for each k the family (T_{k,i})_{i ∈ J_k}.

2. (Diameters.) For every k and every i ∈ J_k, ediam T_{k,i} ≤ r_k by hypothesis; in particular this holds eventually along atTop.

3. (Covering.) Let k ∈ ℕ and x ∈ s. By hypothesis x ∈ T_{k,i} for some i ∈ ℕ. Then T_{k,i} contains x, so it is nonempty, i ∈ J_k, and x ∈ ⋃_{j ∈ J_k} T_{k,j}. Hence s ⊆ ⋃_{j ∈ J_k} T_{k,j} for every k.

4. (Mathlib's covering bound.) Since r_k → 0 and each index type J_k is countable, `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum` (with β = ℕ, the filter atTop, ι k = J_k and the family (k, j) ↦ T_{k,j}) applies to steps 2 and 3 and gives
 μH[d](s) ≤ liminf_{k→∞} Σ_{j ∈ J_k} (ediam T_{k,j})^d.
 (That lemma sums (ediam T)^d without the nonemptiness supremum; this is why empty pieces were discarded in step 1: for d = 0 an empty piece would contribute (ediam ∅)^0 = 1.)

5. (Compare the sums.) Fix k. By `tsum_subtype`, Σ_{j ∈ J_k} (ediam T_{k,j})^d = Σ_{i ∈ ℕ} 1_{J_k}(i)·(ediam T_{k,i})^d, the sum over ℕ of the indicator of the set J_k applied to i ↦ (ediam T_{k,i})^d. Compare termwise (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`): if i ∈ J_k, the i-th term is (ediam T_{k,i})^d = w_d(T_{k,i}) (`le_iSup_of_le` with the proof of T_{k,i} ≠ ∅); if i ∉ J_k, the i-th term is 0 ≤ w_d(T_{k,i}). Therefore Σ_{j ∈ J_k} (ediam T_{k,j})^d ≤ Σ_i w_d(T_{k,i}). (In fact equality holds; only ≤ is needed.)

6. (Pass to liminf.) The bound of step 5 holds for every k, so by monotonicity of liminf (`Filter.liminf_le_liminf` with an eventually-everywhere bound; [0, ∞] is a complete lattice, so no boundedness side conditions are needed), liminf_k Σ_{j ∈ J_k} (ediam T_{k,j})^d ≤ liminf_k Σ_i w_d(T_{k,i}). Combined with step 4 this is the claim. No sign condition on d is needed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reindex each cover by J_k := {i : T_{k,i} ≠ ∅}, a countable type; the reindexed families still cover s and have diameters ≤ r_k.
hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum gives μH[d](s) ≤ liminf_k Σ_{j ∈ J_k} (ediam T_{k,j})^d.
tsum_subtype and a termwise comparison give Σ_{j∈J_k}(ediam T_{k,j})^d ≤ Σ_i ⨆_{T_{k,i}≠∅}(ediam T_{k,i})^d; conclude by liminf_le_liminf.

audit.reason: The type exactly matches the arbitrary-real-exponent statement. Reindexing by nonempty pieces preserves countability, diameter bounds and coverage, including empty index types. The pinned Hausdorff liminf lemma applies without a sign hypothesis on d; subtype summation and liminf monotonicity finish the proof. The empty-piece correction is valid at d = 0 and for negative d.

subproblem.title: Near-optimal small-diameter covers by subsets for a set of finite Hausdorff measure
subproblem.statement: Let X be an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra, let d ∈ ℝ with d ≥ 0, let A ⊆ X be an arbitrary set with μH[d](A) < ∞ (Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure, evaluated as an outer measure), and let r, ε ∈ [0, ∞] with r > 0 and ε > 0. Then there are sets S_i ⊆ A (i ∈ ℕ) with A ⊆ ⋃_i S_i, ediam S_i ≤ r for every i, and Σ_i ⨆_{S_i ≠ ∅} (ediam S_i)^d ≤ μH[d](A) + ε, where ediam is the extended diameter and the supremum over the proposition S_i ≠ ∅ equals (ediam S_i)^d if S_i ≠ ∅ and 0 if S_i = ∅.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℝ) (A : Set X) (r ε : ℝ≥0∞), 0 ≤ d → 0 < r → 0 < ε → (μH[d] : Measure X) A ≠ ∞ → ∃ S : ℕ → Set X, (∀ i, S i ⊆ A) ∧ A ⊆ ⋃ i, S i ∧ (∀ i, ediam (S i) ≤ r) ∧ ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (S i).Nonempty), ediam (S i) ^ d ≤ (μH[d] : Measure X) A + ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. X is an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra. ediam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter `Metric.ediam S` (written `ediam` under `open Metric`); ediam ∅ = 0. μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) sets. Arithmetic is in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0; x^a for x ∈ [0, ∞] and real a is `ENNReal.rpow`. For S ⊆ X and a real exponent a put w_a(S) := ⨆_{S ≠ ∅} (ediam S)^a, the supremum over the proposition S ≠ ∅, so w_a(S) = (ediam S)^a if S ≠ ∅ and w_a(∅) = 0 (in particular w_0(∅) = 0 although (ediam ∅)^0 = 1).

1. (Formula for μH.) By `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply`, μH[d](A) = ⨆_{ρ ∈ (0, ∞]} H_ρ(A), where H_ρ(A) := ⨅ over sequences t : ℕ → Set X with A ⊆ ⋃_n t_n and ediam t_n ≤ ρ for all n of the sum Σ_n w_d(t_n). (The infimum is over t and the two side conditions, i.e. three nested infima.) Since r > 0, taking ρ = r in the supremum gives H_r(A) ≤ μH[d](A) (`le_iSup₂`).

2. (Strict room.) Because μH[d](A) ≠ ∞ and ε > 0, μH[d](A) < μH[d](A) + ε (`ENNReal.lt_add_right`). With step 1, H_r(A) < μH[d](A) + ε.

3. (A good cover.) An infimum that is strictly below a value is attained below that value by some element (`iInf_lt_iff`, applied successively to the three nested infima). Hence there is t : ℕ → Set X with A ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ediam t_n ≤ r for every n, and Σ_n w_d(t_n) < μH[d](A) + ε.

4. (Intersect with A.) Put S_i := t_i ∩ A for i ∈ ℕ. Then S_i ⊆ A. If x ∈ A, then x ∈ t_i for some i by step 3, so x ∈ t_i ∩ A = S_i; hence A ⊆ ⋃_i S_i.

5. (Diameters.) Since S_i ⊆ t_i, ediam S_i ≤ ediam t_i ≤ r (`Metric.ediam_mono`).

6. (Termwise comparison.) For each i, w_d(S_i) ≤ w_d(t_i). Indeed, if S_i = ∅ then w_d(S_i) = 0. Otherwise t_i ⊇ S_i is nonempty, so w_d(t_i) = (ediam t_i)^d, while w_d(S_i) = (ediam S_i)^d ≤ (ediam t_i)^d because ediam S_i ≤ ediam t_i and x ↦ x^d is monotone on [0, ∞] for d ≥ 0 (`ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow`). This is the only place where d ≥ 0 is used.

7. (Sum.) Summing step 6 over i (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`) and using step 3: Σ_i w_d(S_i) ≤ Σ_i w_d(t_i) < μH[d](A) + ε. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: μH[d](A) is the supremum over ρ > 0 of the ρ-content H_ρ(A) (hausdorffMeasure_apply), so H_r(A) ≤ μH[d](A) < μH[d](A) + ε.
iInf_lt_iff gives a countable cover (t_n) of A with ediam t_n ≤ r and Σ w_d(t_n) < μH[d](A) + ε.
S_i := t_i ∩ A still covers A, has ediam ≤ r, and w_d(S_i) ≤ w_d(t_i) because d ≥ 0 (rpow monotone); sum termwise.

audit.reason: The one-line type matches every stated hypothesis and conclusion. The covering formula, strict room from finite measure and positive ε, and successive infimum elimination supply the cover. Intersecting with A preserves coverage and decreases weights using d ≥ 0. Empty pieces, d = 0, and infinite permitted r or ε are handled correctly. No circular dependency.

subproblem.title: Eilenberg's inequality for the unnormalized Hausdorff measure on an arbitrary metric space (constant 2)
subproblem.statement: Let X be an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra, m ∈ ℕ, f : X → ℝ, L ∈ [0, ∞) and A ⊆ X such that f is L-Lipschitz on A. Then there is a Borel function ψ : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ ψ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ and ∫_ℝ ψ dλ¹ ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A). Here μH[k] is Mathlib's unnormalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure on X, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary sets, and λ¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (m : ℕ) (f : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (A : Set X), LipschitzOnWith L f A → ∃ ψ : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable ψ ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, (μH[(m : ℝ)] : Measure X) (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}) ≤ ψ t) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ψ t ≤ 2 * (L : ℝ≥0∞) * (μH[((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)] : Measure X) A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. X is an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra. ediam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter `Metric.ediam S` (written `ediam` under `open Metric`); ediam ∅ = 0. μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) sets. Arithmetic is in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0; x^a for x ∈ [0, ∞] and real a is `ENNReal.rpow`. For S ⊆ X and a real exponent a put w_a(S) := ⨆_{S ≠ ∅} (ediam S)^a, the supremum over the proposition S ≠ ∅, so w_a(S) = (ediam S)^a if S ≠ ∅ and w_a(∅) = 0 (in particular w_0(∅) = 0 although (ediam ∅)^0 = 1). λ¹ = volume on ℝ. f is L-Lipschitz on A: edist(f x, f y) ≤ L·edist(x, y) for x, y ∈ A. The siblings used are near_optimal_cover (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_near_optimal_cover`), liminf_cover_bound (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_liminf_cover_bound`) and cover_majorant (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_cover_majorant`), each applied with the same space X.

1. (Case L = 0.) For x, y ∈ A, edist(f x, f y) ≤ 0·edist(x, y) = 0, so f(x) = f(y). Hence the image f(A) ⊆ ℝ has at most one point; it is a subsingleton, hence countable (`Set.Subsingleton.countable`), hence Borel (`Set.Countable.measurableSet`) and λ¹-null (`Set.Countable.measure_zero`, Lebesgue measure has no atoms). Let ψ be the indicator of f(A) with constant value ∞. It is measurable. If t ∈ f(A), then ψ(t) = ∞ ≥ μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}). If t ∉ f(A), then A ∩ f⁻¹{t} = ∅ (a point x ∈ A with f(x) = t would put t in f(A)), so μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 ≤ ψ(t). Finally ∫ψ dλ¹ = ∞·λ¹(f(A)) = ∞·0 = 0 ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A) (`lintegral_indicator_const`). This settles L = 0; assume L ≠ 0 from now on.

2. (Case μH[m+1](A) = ∞.) Let ψ be the constant function ∞. It is measurable and the pointwise bound is trivial. Since L ≠ 0, 2L ≠ 0, so 2L·∞ = ∞ (`ENNReal.mul_top`) and ∫ψ ≤ ∞ = 2L·μH[m+1](A). Assume μH[m+1](A) ≠ ∞ from now on.

3. (Scales.) For k ∈ ℕ let ρ_k := (k + 1)⁻¹ ∈ [0, ∞] (inverse in [0, ∞] of the cast of k + 1). Then ρ_k > 0 (`ENNReal.inv_pos`, since k + 1 ≠ ∞), and ρ_k → 0 as k → ∞ (`ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero` composed with k ↦ k + 1, `tendsto_add_atTop_nat`).

4. (Covers.) For each k apply near_optimal_cover with d := m + 1 (the real cast of the natural number m + 1; d ≥ 0), the set A, r := ρ_k and ε := ρ_k (both > 0) and μH[m+1](A) ≠ ∞. Choosing for every k (`choose`), we get sets S_{k,i} ⊆ A (k, i ∈ ℕ) with A ⊆ ⋃_i S_{k,i}, ediam S_{k,i} ≤ ρ_k, and Σ_i w_{m+1}(S_{k,i}) ≤ μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k.

5. (Majorants.) For each k apply cover_majorant to m, f, L, A (with the Lipschitz hypothesis) and the family (S_{k,i})_{i ∈ ℕ}, whose members lie in A by step 4. Choosing for every k, we get Borel functions ψ_k : ℝ → [0, ∞] with
 (i) Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ (A ∩ f⁻¹{t})) ≤ ψ_k(t) for every t ∈ ℝ, and
 (ii) ∫ψ_k dλ¹ ≤ 2L·Σ_i w_{m+1}(S_{k,i}) ≤ 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k), the second inequality by step 4 and monotonicity of multiplication by 2L.

6. (The majorant.) Define ψ(t) := liminf_{k→∞} ψ_k(t). It is Borel as the liminf of a sequence of Borel functions (`Measurable.liminf`).

7. (Pointwise bound.) Fix t ∈ ℝ and put B := A ∩ f⁻¹{t}. Apply liminf_cover_bound with d := m (real cast), s := B, the sequence ρ of step 3 (ρ_k → 0) and T_{k,i} := S_{k,i} ∩ B. Its hypotheses hold: ediam T_{k,i} ≤ ediam S_{k,i} ≤ ρ_k (`Metric.ediam_mono`, step 4); and for every k, if x ∈ B then x ∈ A ⊆ ⋃_i S_{k,i}, so x ∈ S_{k,i} ∩ B for some i, i.e. B ⊆ ⋃_i T_{k,i}. Hence μH[m](B) ≤ liminf_k Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ B). By 5(i), Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ B) ≤ ψ_k(t) for every k, so by monotonicity of liminf (`Filter.liminf_le_liminf`) μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ liminf_k ψ_k(t) = ψ(t).

8. (Integral bound.) By Fatou's lemma for measurable functions (`lintegral_liminf_le`), ∫ψ dλ¹ = ∫ liminf_k ψ_k dλ¹ ≤ liminf_k ∫ψ_k dλ¹, and by 5(ii) and monotonicity of liminf this is ≤ liminf_k 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k). The sequence μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k converges to μH[m+1](A) + 0 = μH[m+1](A) (constant plus ρ_k → 0, `Filter.Tendsto.add`), and multiplication by the finite constant 2L (2L ≠ ∞ because L is a finite nonnegative real) preserves this limit (`ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`). A convergent sequence has liminf equal to its limit (`Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq`), so liminf_k 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k) = 2L·μH[m+1](A). Hence ∫ψ dλ¹ ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A), and ψ has all required properties. ∎

Remark. The case analysis mirrors step 6 of the parent proof. The two degenerate cases use explicit majorants (the ∞-valued indicator of the at most one-point set f(A) when L = 0, and the constant ∞ when L ≠ 0 and μH[m+1](A) = ∞), so no covers are needed there; this is why the statement holds on an arbitrary extended metric space without separability.
proof_key_steps: L = 0: f is constant on A; ψ := ∞·1_{f(A)} works since f(A) is countable, hence Borel and λ¹-null.
L ≠ 0 and μH[m+1](A) = ∞: ψ :≡ ∞ works since 2L·∞ = ∞.
Otherwise, for ρ_k = (k+1)⁻¹ take near-optimal covers S_{k,·} of A (near_optimal_cover) and their majorants ψ_k (cover_majorant) with ∫ψ_k ≤ 2L(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k).
ψ := liminf_k ψ_k is Borel; liminf_cover_bound applied to T_{k,i} := S_{k,i} ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹{t} gives μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ ψ(t).
Fatou (lintegral_liminf_le) and convergence of 2L(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k) give ∫ψ ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A).

In the finite-measure case, the three declared dependencies supply shrinking covers, measurable majorants and the pointwise liminf bound; Fatou and multiplication by finite 2L give the integral estimate. Dependencies are correctly directed and acyclic. Instantiating X = Eucl P and scaling by κ_m with C = 2κ_m/κ_{m+1} proves exactly the selected frozen parent.
